appeal.powers: rules on whether the body may withhold, on the body's own request
appeal.sentence: Texas has no free citizen appeal board. If the City wants to withhold, it must ask the Attorney General for a ruling within ten business days (§ 552.301) and send you a copy of what it asked — that request and the ruling are both public, and they are the best record of what a city tried to hide. If the City simply never answers, a complaint goes to the county or district attorney under § 552.3215, or you can sue for mandamus under § 552.321.

issue.headline: A data centre campus with its own power plant, negotiated in closed session
issue.body: Abilene's City Council has spent a year approving tax abatements, site infrastructure agreements and zoning for a data centre campus operated by Lancium, running through numbered companies - Abilene DC 1 and DC 3 to DC 10, each tied to a numbered phase - plus Abilene DC TPP, LLC, which the City's own agenda calls an Electricity Generation Plant. Most of it was discussed first under the business-prospect exception in Texas Government Code 551.087. That is lawful. It also means the negotiation happened in private and the agreements are the only public account of what was agreed.
issue.record: The executed tax abatement agreements and second agreements with Lancium LLC and each Abilene DC entity, the Site Infrastructure Agreements approved 8 January 2026, the ordinance and boundary for Reinvestment Zone RZ25-1 (approximately 614.91 acres), and any water supply or utility service agreement they reference - all held by the City of Abilene.
